full_judgment:
This rule arises out of a miscellaneous case for violation of an order of injunction now pending in the court below. 

 3. It appears that the petitioner filed an application for drawing up appropriate proceedings against the opposite parties for alleged violation of an injunction order and miscellaneous case No. 196 of 1975 was started on 8-11-75. After series of adjournments, the case was finally taken up for exparte hearing on 7-5-77. 

 4. The certified copy of the order sheet annexed to the petition and the procedure adopted by the learned Munsif in the matter reveal a very sad and unfortunate state of affairs. On 7-5-77 the prayer for adjournment by the opposite party was rejected by the learned Munsif and the case was taken up for exparte hearing, petitioner's witnesses were examined and documents filed on behalf of the petitioner were also marked as exhibits. The hearing of evidence of the ease appears to have been concluded and the obvious course for the court was to set it down for arguments "on the following day. But, the case was adjourned for further hearing two weeks hence on 21-5-77, although there appears to be no prayer from the petitioner for adducing further evidence nor was an, reason recorded for not taking lip the case of the following day as required under the law. On 21-5-77, the court entertained an application for adjournment from the opposite  party and adjourned that case to 28-5-77 on which date the opposite party was allowed to cross examine the petitioner's witnesses and again the case was adjourned to 10-6-77 for further hearing. On the said date opposite party's witnesses were examined and evidence was closed and the case was adjourned to 18.6.77 for arguments. On 18.6.77 the arguments were not heard and it was again adjourned to 9-7-77 for arguments. On 9-7-77 only the argument for the petitioner was heard and 16-7-77 was, fixed for argument by the opposite party. The matter was again adjourned to 26-7-77 on which date arguments for the opposite party was heard in part and it was adjourned to 6-8-77 for further argument. On 6-8-77 on argument was heard on the ground that the court was otherwise engaged and the matter was adjourned for about two months to 1-10-77. On the prayer of the petitioner to hear the matter within a week the date appears to have been brought forward by only one day to 30-9-77. On 30-9-77 the matter was again adjourned without hearing for more than two months to 5-12-77. At the time of hearing of the rule the learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that even on 5-12-77 the matter was not taken up for hearing and it was again adjourned but he could not as yet 0btain the next date. It further appears that apart from the allegation of violation of injunction, the petitioner has been consistently praying since 18-6-77 for restoration of his possession in the suit premises from where he is alleged to have been forcibly dispossessed by the defendants during the pendency of the suit. That application was also put off by the learned Munsif without bearing for one reason or the other. 

 (1) The court may, if sufficient cause, is shown, at any stage of the suit grant time to the parties or to any of them, and may from time to time adjourn the hearing of the suit. Costs to adjournment.- (2) In every such case the court shall fix a day for the further hearing of the suit, and may make such order if it thinks fit with respect to the costs occasioned by the adjournment. 

 5. From the above provision of law it appears that once the hearing of the evidence has begun the hearing of the suit must be continued from day to day unless the court finds adjournment of the hearing beyond the following day to be necessary for reasons to be recorded. In the instant case, the learned Munsif had been adjourning the part-heard matter without recording any reason whatsoever and the matter was adjourned not for days but for weeks and on same occasions even beyond two months. This was an unheard of procedure followed by the learned Munsif in utter disregard of the law which was his bounden duty to follow. 

 6. Then again, on 7-5-77 the learned Munsif had taken up the matter for exparte disposal and examination of the witnesses for the petitioner was also concluded. Though the petitioner did not pray for adducing any any further evidence, curiously enough the learned Munsif adjourned the case for further hearing two weeks hence when he should have set it down for arguments on the following day and on the next date he entertained an application for adjournment from the opposite party and allowed the same without setting aside his earlier order of exparte disposal. 

 7. The procedure adopted and followed by the learned Munsif, I am constrained to observe, amounts to clear harassment of the petitioner who had come to seek justice in a court of law and it is clearly an abuse of the discretion vested in the court. Granting of adjournment is no doubt a discretion Vested in the court as is evident from Order 17, rule 1 of the Code but the discretion must be exercised in a judicial and reasonable manner and not arbitrarily or capriciously in which case it is no exercise of discretion in the eye of law. Such arbitrary exercise of discretion may tend to undermine the confidence and respect of the people in administration of justice without which the judiciary cannot properly discharge its duties. The courts should, therefore, be extremely careful in exercising the discretion vested in them and always keep in mind the oft-repeated legal maxim that justice must not only be done but must also appear to be done. Once a matter is part-heard, it must let priority over other pending cases and it was rather unusual for a court to adjourn a part-heard matter on the ground that the court was otherwise engaged. The order sheet also does not show why such long adjournments were allowed in a part-heard matter and that also without any prayer from the parties. The observation I have made, I hope, will be a sufficient warning to the learned Munsifs concerned for their further guidance and any future lapse on their part in the discharge of their judicial functions and duties shall be taken serious note of. 

 8. Having regard to these facts and circumstances, it is directed that the miscellaneous case No. 196 of 1975 and the application filed by the petitioner for restoration of possession be disposed of within 15 days of the receipt of the order by the learned Munsif.
